purpose: Current brief: retro cartridge-game opening animation → pixel-art title screen → gameplay. Same game-native pixel art in every frame.

prompts.title: The House Wakes Up
prompts.prompt:
Create a professional pixel-art storyboard for the opening of NEARlyHuman, an actual retro 16-bit cartridge game, as if booting a Game Boy Advance / Sega-era game.
ONE landscape image, EXACTLY THREE equal portrait gameplay viewports side by side, read left to right. They show successive stages of ONE continuous opening: 1 FIRST VISIBLE INTRO ANIMATION, 2 TITLE SCREEN reached by that animation, 3 START has been pressed and the game begins. Small board heading/scene numbers outside the viewports only.
ABSOLUTELY ALL THREE FRAMES USE THE SAME GENUINE LOW-RESOLUTION PIXEL-ART STYLE as the provided existing game: consistent square pixel scale, stepped sprite outlines, tiled environments, limited shading, charming GBA furniture and small simple pixel rooster. This is not a cartoon illustration or animation concept painting. No smooth drawing, hand-drawn/cel-art rooster, painted scenery, glossy3D or art-style transformation. Intro, logo/title and gameplay all look like assets from the SAME game cartridge.
The reference is a content/style reference for the existing warm wood, navy HUD, top-down house and simple white rooster sprite. Ignore the empty surrounding cream page. The entire portrait viewport is game art in EVERY panel; no webpage chrome, CRT, decorative frame, illustrated surround, game screenshot inside another scene, marketing layout or logo above a small embedded game.
Maintain object positions and spatial continuity between stages. Show the title “NEARlyHuman” in large beautiful pixel lettering in FRAME2, with one small “START” underneath. Frame3 loses that title and introduces the existing compact navy status HUD at top and concise navy dialogue box at bottom; the playable HOUSE FILLS THE WHOLE VIEWPORT, including above and below, in the same overhead perspective as the reference. No new mechanics. Treat this as a short skippable cartridge opening, not a loading screen. Let the reference's pixel art guide all art, not only the last panel.

DIRECTION — THE HOUSE WAKES UP. A snappy magical pixel-tile assembly opening, viewed in EXACTLY THE SAME LOCKED STRAIGHT TOP-DOWN CAMERA THROUGH ALL THREE STAGES. No isometric view anywhere.
Frame1: the actual room is forming at once—wooden floor tiles slide into rows, stove/fridge/bed/table sprites pop out of little pixel-dust puffs into their final locations; enough room exists immediately to feel like the game. The tiny white rooster stands at the same central floor coordinate throughout.
Frame2: those same tiles and sparkles gather into the big NEARlyHuman pixel title floating above the same nearly completed room, with START beneath. Same room, same camera, same furniture locations; this is the TITLE state, not a different scene.
Frame3: title letters dissolve into a few final floor pixels while the compact real HUD arrives. Exactly that room is now gameplay; rooster starts moving toward the fridge. The transformation should be immediately legible: assembling the room → title held over the room → live room. Rich jewel-blue sparkle accents may brighten the intro, but the house's warm pixel-art treatment stays consistent. Keep every element sharply pixelated and simple enough to feel implementable in a GBA game.
Board heading “03 · THE HOUSE WAKES UP”.
